interfaces.name: Nevo OWR 2005
interfaces.interface: Definition 1 fixes a coefficient field and same-dimension vertex deletion. Theorem 7 uses d-dimensional minimal cycle complexes for d≥1, overlaps containing d-faces, with any piece permitted first. Problem 8 asks whether those pieces can be homology spheres.
interfaces.role: Original question; a dimension-two example over Q addresses this universal question.

interfaces.name: Nevo published 2008
interfaces.interface: Definition 3.1; Theorem 3.4 and its proof; Problem 3.7 on printed 417. The later question about Cohen–Macaulay intersections is additional, not a substitute for sphere-piece existence.
interfaces.role: Journal original-question authentication. The arXiv v2 alternate is retained, but this scope relies on the published body.

interfaces.name: Swartz v1
interfaces.interface: Homology spheres require sphere homology globally and in every face link, and are termed Gorenstein* complexes. Theorem 4.1 concerns convex-ear constructions, with a homology-sphere/ball extension.
interfaces.role: Terminology/context; no converse asserting that every 2-CM complex has such a decomposition is imported.

interfaces.name: Lubotzky–Samuels–Vishne v2
interfaces.pages_read: PDF 1–13; in particular Sections 2–4 through Proposition 4.9; rendered Equation (9)/Proposition 4.8 on PDF 13
interfaces.interface: Lattice-chain affine building over a positive-characteristic local field; conjugation embedding into GL_(d²); polynomial ring R0=Fq[1/y]; Corollary 4.6 gives positive words for index q^ell lattices; Definition 4.7 and Equation (9) place Γ in GL_(d²)(R0); Proposition 4.8 gives simple vertex transitivity.
interfaces.role: Load-bearing imported construction, specialized to q=11,d=3. The manuscript reduces the already-defined faithful matrix group modulo t^9; it does not define the cyclic algebra over R0, nor invoke global Ramanujan assertions in Section 6.

interfaces.name: Lubotzky–Meshulam author version
interfaces.interface: Polynomial degree/congruence comparison controls displacement. The source arithmetic quotient uses irreducible h prime to lambda(1+lambda).
interfaces.role: Credited method antecedent, not a theorem applied unchanged to the manuscript’s nonreduced t^9 quotient. The manuscript supplies a direct degree≤8 versus divisibility by t^9 argument.

interfaces.name: Ballmann–Świątkowski MPI96-127
interfaces.pages_read: PDF 3–5 (printed 1–3), with formula context on PDF 12 and 15; theorem interface only, not full 28-page proof
interfaces.interface: Theorem 1 uses locally finite dimension two, connected vertex links and a uniform normalized spectral gap strictly above 1/2; it gives twisted L² H¹ vanishing. PDF 4 explicitly includes the trivial acting group.
interfaces.role: Garland-type antecedent. Finite X has a uniform margin and all cochains are square-integrable; the current manuscript additionally gives its own finite weighted-cocycle proof. No Property (T), contractibility or global building spectrum is needed for its Lemma 2.

interfaces.name: Januszkiewicz–Świątkowski published
interfaces.interface: Example 1.8(5) records the combinatorial curvature obstruction for triangulated two-spheres. The surrounding k-large/full-subcomplex terminology is more specialized than arbitrary subcomplex inclusion.
interfaces.role: Curvature antecedent, not a replacement argument. Manuscript Section 4 directly uses edge links, connected cycle vertex links and an Euler count for any field, including non-induced subcomplexes.

interfaces.name: Larson–Stapledon v2
interfaces.interface: Complementary-vector/Hilbert-function statements use a fixed characteristic-two field, and discuss convex ear decompositions as examples.
interfaces.role: Recent neighboring context only, not an imported construction or proof that this sphere-decomposition question was previously answered. This limited reading is no worldwide priority search.

fresh_alternate_retained.name: Nevo arXiv v2
fresh_alternate_retained.scope: Web first two pages/metadata inspected; not relied upon in place of journal question.

limits: Selective exact-interface reading, not cover-to-cover validation of all cited works. No global-priority conclusion. Reisner criterion is the paper’s explicit homological definition and is also stated by Nevo; the original Reisner article was not separately acquired.
